name: Flanking: +2, not advantage
author: Alexandria
summary: Two allies on opposite sides of a foe each get +2 to hit it, instead of advantage.

rules.text: When you and an ally are on **opposite sides** of a creature and both can act, you each get a **bonus to attack rolls** against it (the GM sets it, +2 by default) instead of advantage. A creature that cannot be flanked (no front or back, or that sees all around) ignores it.

assistant.gm: Flanking at this table is a flat bonus to hit (the rule's option, +2 by default), not advantage. It does not stack with itself.
assistant.player: Flanking at this table gives a flat bonus to hit (usually +2), not advantage. Both attackers need to be on opposite sides of the foe and able to act.
